what: Ferrovial builds and owns infrastructure. It holds a large stake in the 407 toll motorway around Toronto and in managed lanes in Texas and Virginia, owns a share of Heathrow-area airports and others, and runs a construction business that builds the projects.
customers: Drivers paying tolls, air passengers and airlines, and governments awarding construction and concession contracts.
money: the 407 ETR in Toronto and managed lanes in Texas and Virginia
the largest part of revenue, thin margin
stakes in airports in the United Kingdom and elsewhere
moat: Toll concessions with decades left to run on roads that cannot be duplicated, where it sets prices within contractual limits.
risks: Construction margins are thin and projects can go wrong
Debt of about $12 billion sits against long-dated concession assets
Toll traffic falls in a recession
opportunities: Managed lanes in Texas and Virginia raise prices with congestion and have grown faster than forecast
The 407 concession runs to 2098 and raises tolls each year
watch: Traffic and toll revenue on the 407 and the US managed lanes.
